questions.stem: A student mixes citric acid and sodium hydrogencarbonate in a beaker and measures the temperature. The temperature drops from 22°C to 14°C. What type of reaction is this?

options.text: Exothermic, because the chemicals are reacting
Endothermic, because the temperature of the surroundings decreases as energy is absorbed
Exothermic, because energy is being transferred to the surroundings
Neither exothermic nor endothermic, because no flames are produced

questions.explanation: The temperature decrease shows that the reaction is absorbing energy from the surroundings (the solution acts as the surroundings here). This is an endothermic reaction - energy is transferred from the surroundings to the reacting chemicals, causing the temperature to fall. Exothermic reactions cause a temperature increase.

questions.stem: Hand warmers contain iron powder that reacts slowly with oxygen when exposed to air. What energy transfer occurs in this process?

options.text: Energy is absorbed from the surroundings, making the hand warmer cold
Electrical energy is converted to heat energy
Chemical energy is transferred to thermal energy in the surroundings (exothermic)
Kinetic energy of the iron particles produces heat through friction

questions.explanation: The oxidation of iron is an exothermic reaction. Chemical energy stored in the reactants is transferred as thermal energy to the surroundings (your hands). The products have less chemical energy than the reactants, and the difference is released as heat. This is why hand warmers feel warm.

questions.stem: Instant cold packs used for sports injuries contain ammonium nitrate and water in separate compartments. When squeezed, they mix and the pack becomes cold. How does this work?

options.text: The ammonium nitrate freezes the water
Dissolving ammonium nitrate is endothermic - it absorbs heat from the surroundings
The water evaporates and takes heat away
The ammonium nitrate undergoes an exothermic reaction that removes heat

questions.explanation: When ammonium nitrate dissolves in water, the process is endothermic - it absorbs thermal energy from the surroundings. The surroundings (your skin) lose heat energy to the dissolving process, so the pack feels cold. This is a practical application of an endothermic process.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an endothermic reaction?

options.text: Burning methane in a Bunsen burner
Neutralising hydrochloric acid with sodium hydroxide
Thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate
Rusting of iron

questions.explanation: Thermal decomposition requires continuous heating to proceed - energy must be constantly supplied, making it endothermic. Combustion (burning), neutralisation, and oxidation (rusting) are all exothermic reactions that release energy to the surroundings.

questions.stem: In an exothermic reaction, energy is released to the surroundings. In terms of the chemical energy of the reactants and products, which statement is correct?

options.text: The products have more chemical energy than the reactants
The products and reactants have equal chemical energy
The products have less chemical energy than the reactants
Chemical energy is not involved; only thermal energy changes

questions.explanation: In an exothermic reaction, the products have less chemical energy than the reactants. The difference in energy is released to the surroundings as thermal energy (heat). Energy is conserved - the chemical energy lost by the chemicals equals the thermal energy gained by the surroundings.
